newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Exxon to expand Singapore chemical production.
newsitem.headline: Exxon to expand Singapore chemical production.

text.p: Exxon Chemical Company, a division of Exxon Corp, plans to spend Singapore $17.5 million (US$12.5 million) to double the capacity of its calcium sulphonate unit at its Singapore petroleum additive complex, the company said on Monday.
This will make the calcium sulphonate unit the company's biggest worldwide, it said in a statement.

"We see continuing high demand growth across Asia Pacific for higher quality lubricants and with it, increasingly sophisticated additives for those motor oil," said Tom Dance, worldwide manufacturing vice-president of Exxon Chemical's
construction to expand the nine-year old unit's capacity from 15,000 to more than 30,000 tonnes per year, is underway with meachanical completion due late 1997, the statement said.

The Paramins complex, located on Pulau Ayer Chawan, off Singapore's west coast, produces a wide range of fuel and lubricant additives. This include calcium sulphonate which helps to neutralise corrosive acids generated in internal combustion engines.

Exxon, whose calcium sulphonate unit is the only facility of its kind in the Asia Pacific, said demand for the additive has grown by around 10 percent a year and is expected to continue rising at a strong rate.
"By investing in major calcium sulphonate capacity in Singapore, we're gearing up to help saisfy that demand," Dance said.
